_meta.indication: Treatment of adults with cervical dystonia to reduce the severity of abnormal head position and neck pain in both toxin-naive and previously treated patients; and temporary improvement in the appearance of moderate to severe glabellar lines associated with procerus and corrugator muscle activity in adult patients < 65 years of age.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), placebo-controlled, double-blind, multicenter, single-dose study followed by a planned 12-week observation period; Study 45 was conducted only in the US.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with cervical dystonia, both toxin-naive and previously treated patients.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to Week 4 in the Toronto Western Spasmodic Torticollis Rating Scale (TWSTRS) total score.
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant beneficial effect of Dysport 500 Units over placebo in change from baseline in TWSTRS total score at Week 4 (p = 0.013).

nct_ctgov.title: Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study of AbobotulinumtoxinA (Dysport®) for the Treatment of Cervical Dystonia

key_safety: In cervical dystonia placebo-controlled trials, the most commonly reported adverse reactions (>5%) were muscular weakness, dysphagia, dry mouth, injection site discomfort, fatigue, headache, neck pain, musculoskeletal pain, dysphonia, injection site pain, and eye disorders. In the double-blind phase (DYSPORT 500 Units N=173 vs placebo N=182), muscular weakness occurred in 16% vs 4%, dysphagia 15% vs 4%, and injection site discomfort 13% vs 8%. In glabellar lines trials the most frequent events (>=2%) were nasopharyngitis, headache, injection site pain, injection site reaction, upper respiratory tract infection, eyelid edema, eyelid ptosis, sinusitis and nausea.
target_moa: AbobotulinumtoxinA is an acetylcholine release inhibitor and neuromuscular blocking agent; botulinum toxin type A cleaves SNAP-25, inhibiting release of neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) from nerve endings.
modality: Other (botulinum toxin type A biological product; protein neurotoxin)

boxed_warning.content: Distant Spread of Toxin Effect: the effects of DYSPORT and all botulinum toxin products may spread from the area of injection to produce symptoms consistent with botulinum toxin effects; swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death. Risk is probably greatest in children treated for spasticity.

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin and the potential for medication errors related to lack of interchangeability with other botulinum toxin products.

advisory_committee.vote: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because Dysport is not first in its class; its active ingredient is the same as that of Botox, and the pharmacological properties of botulinum toxin Type A are well-established.
